sites.description:
Many may not know that NYPL has a special branch dedicated to serving patrons with print disabilities. The Andrew Heiskell Braille and Talking Book Library provides free accessible reading material for patrons who are blind, visually impaired, or otherwise physically unable to read standard print.

Visitors will step behind the scenes to see the Heiskell Library's professional audiobook studio, where a team of staff and volunteers record audiobooks for the Library of Congress service for blind and print-disabled readers. They'll learn about the program's history and technology and see a demonstration of the recording process in action.

Visitors will also get the chance to explore hands-on what it's like to read and write in Braille, draw by touch using raised-line techniques, and try out technologies used by blind and low-vision people every day.

The Heiskell Library offers materials to borrow in a wide range of formats, including braille, audiobooks, and large print, for users of all ages, as well as audiobook players and mobile apps. Patrons can also find accessible programming and events, individual coaching in assistive technology, group workshops, braille study groups, the Dimensions Lab for tactile creation, and more.
sites.short: Visit a unique public library serving blind and print-disabled readers, tour the professional audiobook studio, try hands-on Braille reading and writing, and explore innovative assistive technologies and tactile creation tools.

sites.description: Experience a self-guided, timed-entry visit to the Edward Hopper Studio, located within New York University's Silver School of Social Work. NYU Silver has preserved this eminent American painter’s studio, where students and faculty who meet in the space are surrounded by artifacts of Hopper’s life: the easel he painted on, the stand for his models, the press for his etchings. The original stove, refrigerator, and gas burner oven are all untouched. On view are portraits of Hopper and his wife by Arnold Newman and Berenice Abbott, both renowned American photographers. The studio also features Hopper reproductions.

sites.name: NYU Grey Art Museum Sustainability Tour
sites.description:
In 2023, NYU completed its renovation of the Grey Art Museum, newly located at 18 Cooper Square and occupying the majority of the first floor and basement. The Grey Art Museum functions to collect, preserve, study, document, interpret, and exhibit the evidence of human culture. The Grey Art Museum has been certified as a LEED Gold building and serves as a model for other NYC buildings seeking to reduce their environmental impact. Join this tour to learn about the facilities and sustainability upgrades made during the museum construction. 

Following the tour at Grey Art Gallery, participants are invited to visit The Latinx Project’s gallery next door, located on the third floor at 20 Cooper Square where "Crossing Relations: Migrations and Possible Worlds" will be on view. Curated by Orlando Ochoa, Jr. and Isabel Saavedra-Weis, Crossing Relations features the work of seven contemporary artists—Chelsea Ramirez, Johana Moscoso, Juana Estrada Hernandez, Juana Valdés, Kevin Quiles Bonilla, Paola de la Calle, and Victoria Martinez—who document the intimate texture of movement and ties across the lands, waters, and skies of Colombia, Cuba, Mexico, Puerto Rico, and regions of the United States.
sites.short: Tour the newly renovated, LEED Gold-certified museum for a behind-the-scenes look at its sustainability upgrades, then view "Crossing Relations," an exhibition highlighting contemporary Latinx artists' perspectives on migration and cultural connections.

sites.description: Visitors will be welcomed through the iron gates of Old Gravesend Cemetery for a tour of the landmark site which is not generally open to the public. Friends of Olmsted-Beil House welcomes OHNY Weekend participants to visit the grounds of the 17th-century farmhouse once owned by landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted, a New York City Landmark that is listed on the New York State and National Register of Historic Places. Visitors will be able to independently walk the grounds of Olmsted’s former Tosomock Farm, now a NYC Park, and view trees planted by Olmsted as early landscape architecture experiments, predating his Central Park designs. 

While the house interior is closed to the public as it undergoes preservation work, Friends of Olmsted-Beil House board members will be on hand to introduce the site and the steps being taken to ensure its survival, including some exciting developments in the past year.

sites.name: One Domino Square
sites.description:
One Domino Square is a 700,000-square-foot mixed-use development designed by Selldorf Architects for Two Trees Management Company at the southernmost point of the historic Domino Sugar refinery site in Williamsburg. The project anchors a new 11-acre public park and sits adjacent to Domino Square, a piazza of open park space. Part of Two Trees’ larger redevelopment of the Domino complex, the project highlights the iconic fabric of the neighborhood while reestablishing the city’s vital waterfront connection.

The building comprises two residential towers atop a shared seven-story podium. The south tower rises 550 feet with 55 floors and 400 residences, while the north tower rises 450 feet with 39 floors and 160 residences. Apartments range from studios to four bedrooms, with views overlooking the East River, Midtown Manhattan, the city’s three iconic bridges, downtown Brooklyn, and Lower Manhattan.

The towers are clad in an iridescent, pearl-like porcelain tile that reflects the sky, creating a continually changing, animated effect on the façades. The podium is defined by light grey granite, reflective glass, and large windows, extending the building’s luminous character and creating a layered relationship with the surrounding public spaces.

Residential amenities occupy the podium and include a fitness center and aquatic suite, children’s playroom, coworking space, and multi-sport simulators. Landscaped terraces provide additional spaces for gathering, with an outdoor pool, lounge areas, and semi-private entertaining spaces overlooking the park.
sites.short: Explore a new mixed-use development designed by Selldorf Architects for Two Trees Management Company at the historic Domino Sugar refinery, with views overlooking the city skyline and three iconic East River bridges.

sites.name: One Madison Avenue
sites.description:
One Madison Avenue is one of New York’s most ambitious adaptive reuse projects: a transformation that adds a 14-story glass tower atop the retained podium of a 1960s office building, it preserves the relationship to the landmarked Metropolitan Life clock tower next door.

The tour walks through the design and engineering behind that transformation. Visitors will see how the team kept 67% of the original structure, including the Alabama limestone podium façade, while inserting thirteen concrete mega columns and a new core to carry the tower above.  Participants will walk through the podium’s restored limestone base, the new steel tower with its side-core layout and column-free floor plates, and the garden floors overlooking Madison Square Park. The tour also covers the sequencing challenge of demolishing and rebuilding while keeping the neighboring clock tower hotel fully operational.

This tour will be co-led by KPF Director and Project Manager, Andrew Werner, AIA, and KPF Senior Associate Principal and Project BIM Lead, Chandler Archbell, AIA, offering a rare look at how a mid-century office building became a Class-A headquarters tower without losing its history.
sites.short: Learn the story behind a major architectural transformation, exploring restored limestone facades and exclusive access to the garden level on this tour led by the project’s lead architect.

sites.description:
One Times Square, originally built in 1904 as the headquarters of The New York Times and historically the home of the New Year’s Eve Ball, is now open to the public with unforgettable NYC experiences for all ages. Three unique experiences invite you to learn about Times Square and see an icon of New York City from a new perspective: Times Travel, the Ball Experience, and a Skywalk tour with S9 Architecture.

**5:00-7:00 PM - Times Travel:** Take an interactive trip through the history of Times Square! Virtually ride an airship above Manhattan, hail a time-traveling taxi, and celebrate New Year's Eve 365 days a year in Eternal Midnight. Your journey ends on the Skywalk, 360º viewing deck 19 stories above The Crossroads of the World.

**5:15-6:15 PM - Ball Experience**: This never-before-seen experience invites you to view the New Year's Eve Ball up close, take photos, and learn more about the history behind this NYC icon.

Younsung will discuss S9's design process and the use of the facade as "armature" supporting a dialogue between elevated plaza and public space across the Square.

sites.description: New York City's Borough Presidents are responsible for maintaining the official maps of their respective boroughs. During OHNY Weekend, the Manhattan Borough President's Topographical Bureau will display segments of a historically essential map in the development of Manhattan, executed by John Randel Jr. in 1820. Park Haven is a 178-home affordable housing community developed and operated by The Community Builders in Mott Haven. This mixed-use development brings together affordable and supportive housing, wellness-oriented amenities, sustainable design, workforce development programming and neighborhood-serving retail, including a full-service FRESH grocery store. The tour will offer visitors a firsthand look at how affordable housing can function as civic infrastructure, not only as a place to live, but as a community where thoughtful design, supportive services, resident leadership and neighborhood investment come together. 

Visitors may tour shared spaces including the community room, landscaped terrace, wellness-oriented amenities, a model unit and areas connected to resident programming. The experience will also include a discussion of the project’s design, sustainability features, affordability goals, and role in the Mott Haven neighborhood, as well as The Community Builders’ Community Life approach and resident-led programming.

Tours will be led by The Community Builders team members Kristin Nelson, Director of Design and Construction, Danel Roy, Community Manager, and Brian Dennis, Community Life Service Coordinator.

sites.name: Pellettieri Stone Carvers' Academy Workspace
sites.description:
New York City's character has been defined to a large extent by the work of stone carvers. St. Patrick's Cathedral, Bethesda Terrace, St. John the Divine, and the New York Public Library are fantastic examples, as are the facades of thousands of uncelebrated brownstones and apartment buildings all over town. The industry that created this unique character has disappeared, and the craft of stone carving is a complete mystery to most New Yorkers today. 

During OHNY Weekend, visit the workshop of the only local organization dedicated to promoting and teaching the (almost) lost art of stone carving. Visitors will see demonstrations—the chips will fly—and have a chance to give it a try themselves.
sites.short: Experience live stone carving demonstrations and try your hand at this nearly lost craft in the workshop of the city's only organization dedicated to preserving and teaching traditional stone carving.

sites.name: Pissarro Allaux Studio
sites.description:
Step inside the working studio of multidisciplinary artists Lyora Pissarro and Oliver Allaux, where painting, light, and technology converge to create immersive, dreamlike landscapes.

The studio brings together two distinct multigenerational artistic lineages. Lyora Pissarro is a fifth-generation painter descended from French Impressionist Camille Pissarro, carrying a tradition of landscape painting into a contemporary practice shaped by color, perception, nature, and light. Oliver Allaux comes from a multigenerational family of artists, following in the footsteps of his father, Jean-François Allaux, a French-American artist and editorial illustrator whose work appeared for decades in leading publications including The New York Times.

Together, Lyora and Oliver explore the meeting point between traditional image-making and emerging technology. Oil paintings, digital imagery, projection mapping, and light installations become part of an evolving visual language, transforming static landscapes into immersive environments.

During OHNY Weekend, visitors are invited behind the scenes into their working studio to experience the ideas, materials, experiments, and processes that shape their work. The open studio offers a rare glimpse into how a painting develops from a traditional hand-painted landscape into a multidimensional experience through projected light, movement, and technology.

At its heart, the studio is a space where artistic heritage meets experimentation—honoring the enduring language of landscape while imagining new ways for painting to be experienced.
sites.short: Visit a working studio of two artists from renowned multigenerational lineages to witness how traditional landscape painting evolves into immersive, multidimensional experiences through emerging technologies.

Sporting intimate spaces and welcoming staff, it’s the perfect place to visit—whether solo, with friends or colleagues, or with kids in tow!

sites.description:
On October 17 and 18, Powerhouse Arts will open its doors as part of Open House New York Weekend and Arts Gowanus Open Studios, offering visitors a rare behind-the-scenes look at the creative production spaces that shape the organization. Attendees are invited to move through the Fabrication Shops and Community Studios, including Ceramics, MGC, Print, Public Art, and the Digital Print Lab, to meet our team and creative communities. In addition to self-guided tours, attendees are encouraged to visit for free, drop-in programming on Saturday (Crafternoons) and Sunday (Conversations + Open Studios) to make art in community or learn more about PHA's artist programs!
 
Powerhouse Arts, a not-for-profit organization committed to creative expression, stewarded the redevelopment of the former Brooklyn Rapid Transit Power Station in Gowanus to create a new facility that houses fabrication facilities for ceramics, large metals, print, public art, and textiles. The building— designed by Herzog & de Meuron in collaboration with PBDW Architects— re-imagines the historic power plant as a new art center that meets the multidisciplinary needs of the contemporary arts ecosystem, with multi-use facilities for events, exhibitions, and education.

sites.name: Prime Produce
sites.description:
Tucked away on a quiet block just off Restaurant Row, Prime Produce is a rare thing in Midtown: a standalone, cooperatively owned guildhall built entirely for the common good. It's a "Guild for Good," a modern revival of the medieval guild, reimagined as an intentional community where creatives, nonprofits, educators, and entrepreneurs pool their resources to serve their neighbors.

The ~7,000-square-foot building is notable not for a marquee architect, but for the intention behind every square foot. This is a thoughtfully designed, ADA-accessible space that members don't merely work in; they cooperatively own and govern it, caring for the guildhall (as one co-founder puts it) "like a living thing."

During OHNY Weekend, visitors can explore floor by floor: the ground-level event hall, which hosts everything from symposiums to fashion shows; Cafe 424 by Chef Mom & home to Simple Brewing, serving warm Jamaican cuisine along with stellar local brewed beers; a second-floor co-working commons, conference rooms, classroom, and cybernetics library; and Fresh Produce Studio on the third floor, a home for audio and music-based projects. Participants might even meet the resident rescues of Earthlings NYC, our urban turtle-rehabilitation project.

Learn how a real cooperative runs, and how neighbors gather here for Noodle Nights, screenings, performances, and the beloved New Year's "Shell Drop." Prime Produce's role is to steward and host the friends, family, and neighbors who keep this guildhall humming as a home for anyone building a kinder, more creative New York. Come see what the co-op grows together.
sites.short: Tour a unique, cooperatively owned guildhall where members govern and care for the space, explore event halls, co-working areas, a music studio, and a cybernetics library, enjoy Jamaican cuisine and local brews, and meet the famous rescued turtles.

sites.partner: New York City Department of Parks & Recreation

address.note: Enter at Willoughby Avenue and Washington Park.

sites.description:
During OHNY Weekend, visitors can view the interior of the Prison Ship Martyrs’ Monument, a war memorial at Fort Greene Park that commemorates more than 11,500 American prisoners of war who died in captivity aboard British prison ships during the American Revolutionary War—more than were killed in all the war's other battles, combined. The remains of a small fraction of those who died on the ships are interred in a crypt beneath its base. Rangers will lead tours of the monument (which is not generally open to the public) and also discuss Fort Greene Park’s long history, from its Revolutionary War roots to being an essential downtown green space today for the Fort Greene Community. The monument is a true beacon of Brooklyn.

Rangers will be on site to give first-come, first-served tours on a rolling basis. Visits last about 10 minutes and will be offered every 10 minutes.
sites.short: Step inside the rarely opened monument for ranger-led tours exploring its historic crypt and the powerful story of Revolutionary War prisoners, along with insights into Fort Greene Park's evolution and community significance.

sites.description:

Located within a 10-minute walk of over 244,000 people, and in a high-density area lacking connectivity, the QueensWay will emerge as a thriving open space and greenway. Tours will be led by John Surico, Executive Director of Friends of the QueensWay.

sites.name: Radix Printing & Publishing Cooperative
sites.description:
Radix is a Black-led, worker-owned, union print shop and publisher in Brooklyn, combining a working production shop with an independent press dedicated to underrepresented authors and artists. The shop produces offset, letterpress, and digital print work alongside its publishing program, putting Radix's cooperative, worker-owned model into practice as both a working business and a publishing platform.

During OHNY Weekend, visitors can tour the shop, try hand-setting and printing a letterpress poster, and browse books, stationery, and posters produced in house.

sites.name: Red Hook Treehouses
sites.description:
The Treehouses project is a newly constructed, four-townhouse development in Red Hook that challenges the standard practices of speculative home development by prioritizing neighborhood context, sustainable building methods, and forward-thinking design. This architecturally significant project stands as one of the first heavy timber townhouse developments in New York City, and the very first of its kind in Red Hook. The homes were designed to integrate seamlessly with NYC flood zone requirements and aim to achieve a higher standard for future flood events. Further emphasizing its connection to the environment, the building's footprint was carefully shaped around a 120-year-old silver maple tree, and natural materials are utilized throughout the property.

During OHNY Weekend, tour the Treehouses with Architect and Developer Ben Krone of Gradient Architecture.
sites.short: Experience innovative and architecturally unique timber townhouses designed around a 120-year-old silver maple tree, featuring flood-resilient construction and environmentally conscious materials.

sites.name: Renee & Chaim Gross Foundation
sites.description: In 1963, renowned American sculptor Chaim Gross and his wife Renee converted an art storage warehouse in Greenwich Village into their home and studio. They added a sculpture studio to the ground floor, which is illuminated by an enormous skylight that underwent extensive restoration work in 2017-18. The first floor showcases work spanning Gross’s entire career in both the studio and the adjacent gallery. The second floor houses an intimate temporary exhibition space. On the third floor, see how the Gross family lived surrounded by their global, world-class art collection in their historic, salon-style installation of African, American, European, and Pre-Columbian collections.
sites.short: Uncover a hidden Greenwich Village gem: the home and studio of a celebrated sculptor, featuring a skylit workspace, galleries displaying his life’s work, and a world-class collection rarely seen by the public.

Participants will embark on a guided walk that will meander through local businesses and pathways leading to green space, ultimately culminating in a performance and picnic potluck at Highland Park's Ridgewood Reservoir. Along the way, attendees will engage in interactive journaling exercises, identifying the unique "Sound Marks" of each location and contributing to the creation of a participatory musical composition inspired by the neighborhood's diverse sonic landscape. This project not only celebrates the richness of the community's cultural tapestry but also sheds light on areas requiring improvement, such as disability accessibility and pedestrian safety infrastructure.

Music composed by Concetta Abbate. Music Composition commissioned by Queens Foundation of the Arts. Additional support provided by the Myrtle Avenue Business Improvement District.

sites.partner: NYC Department of Transportation, Rockaway Initiative for Sustainability and Equity (RISE), and Living City Project (LCP)
sites.description:
Rockaway Wellness Way is an evolving civic and cultural gathering place underneath and adjacent to the elevated A train at Beach 59th/60th streets in Far Rockway, Queens. Unmistakably, the “El-Space” is at the crossroads of New York City's transportation infrastructure, coastal ecology, neighborhood identity, and climate adaptation. During OHNY Weekend, residents, designers, artists, engineers, ecologists, students, local organizations, and policymakers will engage to envision Rockaway Wellness Way as a national model for resilient public infrastructure and open space.

Starting at 9:30 AM, the full-day event will feature a multifaceted program of civic design, art, mobility, sustainability, climate resilience and environmental justice centered around a celebratory communal planting activity and evolving into a “living laboratory” where ideas will be developed through gallery exhibitions, artistic interventions, design workshops, and interdisciplinary dialogues—including a live music performance.

The outdoor and indoor happening will be a civic workshop where residents, artists, designers, transportation professionals, environmental advocates, youth groups and public agencies collectively plant, design, experience and celebrate the Rockaway peninsula. The celebration will center around four central activities to engage visitors and participants:

MAKE → IMAGINE → CONNECT → CELEBRATE

sites.description:
Rocking the Boat's campus sits on the edge of one of the most industrial sections of the Bronx, in a corner of Hunts Point. Sandwiched between the Food Market, which supplies 70% of the fresh food New York consumes, and an aggregate and metal recycling facility, and abutting Hunts Point Riverside Park, Rocking the Boat serves middle and high school students through a suite of after-school programs that engage them in environmental science, sailing, and wooden boat building. Rocking the Boat provides a unique youth development opportunity.

As an equity-focused organization, Rocking the Boat also maintains a commitment to providing access to the Bronx River to the larger community. Among other services, community rowing and sailing are offered to the public on Saturdays in the summer. 

Visitors to Rocking the Boat for OHNY Weekend will have the opportunity to tour the facility and Hunts Point Riverside Park as well as embark on a rowing excursion on the Bronx River. Participants will learn a brief ecological history of the river as well as have an opportunity to track bird life.

sites.description:
Join a guided tour of the Roy Lichtenstein Studio, presented by the Whitney Museum of American Art during OHNY Weekend. This intimate program explores the connection between art, place, and New York City through one of the twentieth century's most influential American artists.

Participants will learn about Lichtenstein’s ties to New York, the studio’s history, and the Whitney’s role in preserving American art and artist spaces. The tour provides context for the Whitney's upcoming Roy Lichtenstein exhibition, highlighting creative practices, architectural environments, and the city's cultural fabric.

Designed for those interested in art, design, preservation, and local history, this behind-the-scenes experience offers insights into a space rarely open to the public. It encourages reflection on the role of artists' studios in telling New York’s story as an artistic hub.

Taught by Whitney Teaching Fellow, Caitlin Chan, an art history Ph.D. candidate at Stanford with experience at Columbia, the College Art Association, the Association for Art History, and Leuphana University. She has received the Jeanette and William Hayden Jones Fellowship and previously worked at the Hirshhorn Museum, Gallery 102, and Christie’s.
sites.short: Tour the rarely accessible studio of an iconic 20th-century artist to explore his creative process, the studio’s history, and its significance in New York’s art scene, guided by an expert art historian from the Whitney Museum.

sites.name: Sail Central Park by Rocking the Boat
sites.partner: Sail Central Park and Rocking the Boat
sites.description:
Sail Central Park is located on the park’s Conservatory Water, one of the most iconic model boat sailing venues in the world. Situated between 72nd and 76th streets just west of 5th Avenue, “the Pond” has been a site for model boat sailing since the 1860s. Inspired by the Grand Basin model boat pond in Paris' Luxembourg Gardens, the Conservatory Water was originally called the “Ornamental Water” and was intended to complement a large greenhouse displaying tropical plants. When funding constraints scotched plans for the building, the pond began attracting model boaters who recognized its design as ideal for sailing.

On the eastern shore of the Conservatory Water sits the Kerbs Memorial Boathouse, designed by architect Aymar Embury II. The 1954 boathouse is built in the Georgian style in red brick with a copper hip roof and steeple. Kerbs houses both the Sail Central Park concession, where the public can rent radio-controlled sailboats, and the historic Central Park Model Yacht Club. Founded in 1916, the Club has been a champion of model yachting in America since its inception. 

Sail Central Park is run by Rocking the Boat, a Bronx-based youth development non-profit that engages middle and high school students from the South Bronx in programs in marine science, sailing, and wooden boat building. Sail Central Park is run by a full team of Rocking the Boat alumni who are thrilled to be able to deliver a great small boat experience to the general public.
sites.short: Learn about more than a century of model boat sailing and tour a historic boat house operated by a local nonprofit.
sites.special:
**Friday Activities: **12–4 PM, ongoing.
Visitors to Sail Central Park for OHNY Weekend will tour the Kerbs Boathouse and have the chance to join a photo-guided discussion of the history of model boat sailing in Central Park, from Stuart Little to the present, plus a demonstration of how modern radio-controlled sailboats work. Model sailboat rental is available for a fee.

sites.name: Samaritan Daytop Village Highbridge Development
sites.partner: Samaritan Daytop Village, Mega Contracting Group, and Magnusson Architecture & Planning PC
sites.description:
Highbridge is an award-winning, mixed-use development offering permanent affordable, supportive, and transitional housing for low- to moderate-income families and individuals, formerly homeless residents with supportive service needs, and homeless families with children. Located adjacent to the historic High Bridge, the project includes 316 units of permanently affordable housing and 106 family transitional units, alongside a 5,000-square-foot ground-floor community facility, rooftop gardens, landscaped trails, and 100 new permanent staff positions providing on-site services and 24/7 security.

Now about 85% complete, Highbridge is designed to achieve Passive House and Enterprise Green Communities certification through full electrification and a suite of sustainable systems: heat pump hot water heaters with wastewater heat recovery, VRF heating and cooling, energy recovery ventilators, a large solar PV system, EV charging stations, and a real-time energy monitoring system to track consumption and inform maintenance.

Structurally, the building is a cast-in-place concrete tower using low embodied-carbon concrete mixes, clad in brick and metal rainscreen panels with triple-glazed UPVC windows and thermally broken aluminum storefronts. The landscape design preserves the site's existing woodland and a portico from the former convent, incorporating a trail and elevated walkway with viewing platforms to encourage access to nature and interaction among residents.

During OHNY Weekend, join Jerry Mascuch, Vice President of Real Estate at Samaritan Daytop Village, for a tour led in collaboration with Magnusson Architecture & Planning and Mega Contracting. Visitors will see how the building's sustainable systems, low-carbon construction, and landscape design come together to support both environmental performance and community life, and learn how the project balances affordable and supportive housing with the preservation of the site's historic and natural features.
sites.short: Tour innovative affordable and supportive housing featuring advanced sustainable systems, preserved historic elements, and landscaped trails, and see how design choices foster both environmental performance and vibrant community life.

Highbridge is an active construction site and is not wheelchair accessible. Access to the building is via an uneven gravel path.  

Visitors must be 18+.

sites.name: Second Presbyterian Church NYC
sites.description:
In 1929, Second Presbyterian was among the first churches in the City to partner with a developer to replace its 1890s buildings with a complex including worship spaces, meeting rooms and classrooms, a gym (complete with a bowling alley), and residential apartments, working with renowned architect Rosario Candela. Original 1928 Candela blueprints will be on view during OHNY Weekend. 

The church will also be hosting a dialogue featuring the Executive Director of Graham, a social service agency named for Isabella Graham, an early congregant of the church. The eponymous Graham collaborated with Catherine (Katy) Ferguson, who first came to the Old Scotch Church, as Second Presbyterian was known, in 1793 as an enslaved teenager and went on to become a full communing member of the church. Katy established what is recognized as the first Sunday School in the newly formed United States. The program will discuss the groundbreaking work of these women and their partnership across differences, with a lasting impact today. 

This is the church's 270th anniversary year, and special exhibitions will highlight various eras of its history. The congregation was founded in 1756 and maintains a deep connection to the church's Scottish roots. Eagle-eyed visitors will spot thistles featured in the architectural detail and design, along with the flags of Scotland and the City of Edinburgh in the sanctuary. The founding pastor, John Mason, and his son, John Mitchell Mason, who succeeded him, fostered a spirit of freedom and forward-looking thought still alive today. It was the younger Mason who welcomed Katy Ferguson to join the church; he also went on to help found Union Theological Seminary adjacent to the Columbia University campus.
sites.short: View original 1928 Rosario Candela blueprints, explore special exhibitions marking 270 years of history, and join a dialogue on the pioneering partnership of Isabella Graham and Katy Ferguson, whose work shaped early social services and education.

Secret Riso Club believes in the power of art, design, and independent publishing as tools for collective action and social change. We see creativity as a force for building relationships, exchanging knowledge, and imagining new possibilities. Shared resources, grassroots support, and alternative economic models create the conditions for artists, designers, and communities to thrive together.

Secret Riso Club (SRC) is an artist-run hybrid bookstore, print studio, design practice, and community space dedicated to independent publishing, creative education, and cultural exchange. Their multidisciplinary practice encompasses graphic design, print production, publishing, exhibitions, education, and community-centered cultural programming.

SRC works with artists, designers, publishers, nonprofits, and cultural organizations to develop thoughtful printed matter, programming, and events that explore art, publishing, and community building.

During OHNY Weekend, visit their space in Brooklyn, which features a bookstore with a curated selection of zines & books by independent publishers from around the world, a gallery and reading room, workshop & event space, and a fully equipped print studio. 

Secret Riso Club is run in collaboration between Gonzalo Guerrero and Tara Ridgedell.

sites.name: Skyspace at Friends Seminary
sites.description:
Perched above Friends Seminary’s 16th Street campus, _Leading_ (2023) is a James Turrell Skyspace and a place for silence, reflection, and shared experience. Its name refers to a Quaker “leading”: an inner conviction that guides a person to act. Turrell, a Quaker artist who once worshiped at the nearby 15th Street Meetinghouse, created the work for a school whose mission calls on students to help bring about a world that ought to be.

Visitors sit along the perimeter of a carefully proportioned chamber, surrounded by light that changes slowly enough to make each shift in color feel surprising. During sunset programs, a sharply defined opening in the roof frames the sky while colored light changes how visitors perceive its depth and hue. The experience unfolds through the interaction of the space, the light, and each viewer’s perception. 

For OHNY Weekend, Friends Seminary will present _Leading_’s Closed Dome program. With the roof aperture closed, the convex dome above visitors shifts color in concert with the lighting inside the chamber, creating a distinct experience of Turrell’s work.
sites.short: Experience _Leading, _a James Turrell Skyspace created for silence, reflection, and shared experience perched atop a school whose mission calls on students to help bring about a world that ought to be.

sites.name: Sniffen Court & the Amateur Comedy Club
sites.description:
Step into a hidden corner of New York City’s past with a rare opportunity to explore the Amateur Comedy Club (founded 1884) building and Sniffen Court. Tucked away on East 36th Street, this mid-19th-century mews feel like a secret world within the city. Its ten brick carriage houses, arranged around a quiet courtyard, form the Sniffen Court Historic District, a unique example of 1850s design listed on the National Register of Historic Places. 

During the tour, you’ll discover the Amateur Comedy Club, which transformed two of these carriage houses into a theater in 1918. As the oldest continuously operating theatrical club of its kind in the country, the Club offers a glimpse into history through its Green Room, Prohibition-era liquor lockers, and remarkable collection of theatrical art and memorabilia.

Guests will also enjoy refreshments and a surprise performance.
sites.short: Explore a rarely accessible 19th-century carriage house amid a residential enclave and historic district, home to the historic Amateur Comedy Club, with exclusive access to the Green Room, Prohibition-era liquor lockers, theatrical memorabilia, and a surprise performance.

sites.description:

Rangers will lead tours of the monument, which has undergone significant preservation, including recent restoration work by the Prospect Park Alliance. Visitors can ascend three flights of stairs to view the "Trophy Room" located in the space above the archway. Tours will discuss the history of the arch, the Brooklyn regiments commemorated there who served during the Civil War, and the ongoing effort to preserve the memorial for future generations. 

Tours from 10 AM to 12 PM will be led by David Yum, the architect of the Arch's restoration and Director of Architecture + Preservation at Prospect Park Alliance. Tours from 12 PM onward will be led by Robert Bradfield, Urban Park Ranger.

Please note that the tours will not include access to the outdoor roof terrace of the Soldiers' and Sailors' Memorial Arch.

sites.name: SOM New York Studio at 7 World Trade Center
sites.description:
At the heart of the World Trade Center, SOM’s New York studio occupies two interconnected floors of 7 World Trade Center, the first building erected at the site after September 11, 2001. Following the 25th anniversary of 9/11, the studio tour offers an opportunity to reflect on the rebuilding of Lower Manhattan and the role architecture can play in shaping what comes next. 

For decades, SOM has designed cutting-edge workplaces with the conviction that architecture has the power to shape an organization’s culture. For their own space in New York City, the firm took the opportunity to demonstrate what a forward-looking workplace can be. This 80,000-square-foot studio fosters collaboration and community with a focus on four main tenets: openness, mobility, sustainability, and wellness.

The studio is a piece of industrial design unto itself: an expansive, flexible space characterized by healthy materials, a responsible use of resources, and a focus on sustainability and wellbeing. SOM approached the design through a philosophy known as “radical reduction”—no specification was self-referential or unnecessary. The goal was to holistically integrate the distinct programmatic requirements of a design firm’s office into a refined and tranquil interior.

During OHNY Weekend, participants will join Neil Katz, Associate Principal, and Samuel Wilson, Associate, for a tour of SOM's New York Studio. Visitors will have the opportunity to learn more about SOM's design philosophy of radical reduction; discover the dynamic lighting and shade system that maximizes natural light; and examine indoor air quality sensors that have tracked real-time levels of safe pollutants in the midst of COVID and wildfire smoke.
sites.short: Learn about the “radical reduction” philosophy of a leading architecture studio and see advanced features like dynamic lighting systems and real-time air quality monitoring.

sites.name: Sotheby's After-Hours Tour
sites.description:
Designed by Bauhaus architect Marcel Breuer and completed in 1966 for the Whitney Museum of American Art, the Breuer Building was conceived as a challenge to conventional American museum design, with its inverted ziggurat form, cantilevered granite, and sculptural concrete façade. Since the Whitney's move downtown in 2015, the building has housed the Metropolitan Museum of Art and, later, the Frick Collection during its Fifth Avenue renovation, cementing its status as a cornerstone of New York's cultural landscape. It's now home to Sotheby's, the international auction house, which continues the building's legacy as a home for major art institutions.

On these special after-hours tours during OHNY Weekend, participants will have the chance to tour the building after it closes to the public, and get exclusive insight into the Sotheby's operation.

sites.description:
Take a special guided tour of the flagship of the South Street Seaport Museum’s fleet. Walk the length of the vessel’s massive cargo hold, which is not usually open to the public. 

Built of riveted wrought iron, the 1885 tall ship Wavertree is an archetype of the sailing ships of the latter half of the 19th century that, during the “age of sail,” lined South Street by the dozens, creating a forest of masts from the Battery to the Brooklyn Bridge. 

Guided by Museum Educator Ian Goza, with additional staff and crew, participants will visit areas of the ship that are not typically accessible to the general public. Get a glimpse of how the historic fleet is maintained, see nooks and crannies, and get immersed in history while walking the entire length of Wavertree’s hold.

sites.description:
During OHNY Weekend, visitors are invited to tour Sparrow, a modern funeral home in Greenpoint, Brooklyn. Guests will have the chance to explore the thoughtfully designed space, learn about Sparrow's contemporary approach to funerals, and see how Sparrow is reimagining what it means to gather, grieve, and celebrate a life.

sites.description:
The original St Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church was completely destroyed when the South Tower fell on September 11th, 2001. Reimagined by renowned Spanish architect Santiago Calatrava, the design for its new home was inspired by Byzantine landmarks, specifically the Hagia Sophia and the Church of the Savior in Istanbul. 

Today the building is clad in thin, luminous Pentelic white marble—the exact same stone used to build the ancient Parthenon in Athens. It features a glowing, translucent central dome with 40 windows and 40 ribs that appears solid by day, while radiating a warm, lantern-like glow from within at night.

**Please note:** the building will close from 5-6:30 PM on Friday between its regular drop-in hours and the lighting talk with DLR Group.
sites.short: Experience a stunning architectural revival featuring a glowing marble dome inspired by Byzantine masterpieces, with 40 windows and ribs that create a radiant lantern effect at night, and attend a lecture on the shrine's lighting design.

sites.name: St. Bartholomew's Church
sites.description:
Tour St. Bartholomew’s Church, a National Historic Landmark designed by Bertram Goodhue in 1918. Combining Byzantine and Romanesque styles, the church often surprises visitors who mistake this Episcopal church for a Catholic or Eastern Orthodox parish.

See the impressive triple portal, commissioned by the Vanderbilt family and designed by McKim, Mead & White in 1903, as well as exquisite, glittering mosaics and stained glass by Hildreth Meière, and a magnificent 24-foot-wide Sanctus window designed by Reynolds, Francis and Rohnstock in 1943. Other highlights include a page from a Gutenberg Bible, a baptismal font by Bertel Thorvaldsen, and NYC’s largest pipe organ, an Æolian-Skinner with 12,422 pipes.

St. Bartholomew’s Church is a welcoming and affirming community that brings life to a historic space. Nestled among the city’s high-rises, the church offers a quiet refuge in the heart of Manhattan. View how history, art, and faith come together in this peaceful setting.
sites.short: Explore a stunning blend of Byzantine and Romanesque architecture, marvel at glittering mosaics and rare stained glass, and see treasures like a Gutenberg Bible page and NYC’s largest pipe organ—all in a peaceful, historic sanctuary.

The Stapleton neighborhood of Staten Island is a historical palimpsest. Its layers span maritime and naval history dating to the early 19th century, free-standing Victorian homes and historic row houses from the same era, the oldest African American church in the borough, the Makers Space complex on the waterfront, and a vibrant contemporary street art scene.

With Mary-Beth Shine of SHINE NYC ART, explore the neighborhood where Cornelius Vanderbilt grew up and ferried passengers and goods to Manhattan, and that later gave birth to hip hop innovators the Wu-Tang Clan.

sites.name: Starrett-Lehigh Building
sites.description:
Built in 1931, the Starrett-Lehigh Building is a New York City landmark and one of Manhattan’s most distinctive examples of industrial architecture. Occupying an entire city block between West 26th and 27th Streets and 11th and 12th Avenues, the 2.3-million-square-foot building was designed as a revolutionary vertical manufacturing and distribution hub, with freight elevators large enough to transport trucks directly to upper floors.

Nearly a century later, Starrett-Lehigh has evolved alongside its West Chelsea neighborhood while preserving the architectural character that has made it an icon. Today, the building is home to a dynamic community spanning fashion, media, design, technology, and other creative industries, complemented by more than 100,000 square feet of amenities, dining, event spaces, and gathering places.

During OHNY Weekend, visitors will have the opportunity to experience spaces that are typically reserved for the building’s tenant community and their guests. The tour will explore Starrett-Lehigh’s history and architecture, its transformation from an industrial powerhouse into a modern workplace destination, and the ways its original design continues to influence how the building is used today.

Visitors will also discover how RXR has approached the building’s ongoing evolution—celebrating its history while introducing new spaces, experiences, and amenities designed to foster connection, creativity, and community. Tours will also be led by members of STUDIOS Architecture.
sites.short: Go behind the scenes in rarely accessible areas of this iconic industrial building, exploring its unique architecture, rich history, and transformation into a vibrant creative hub, where original design features shape its modern use.

sites.description:
In the early hours of June 28, 1969, a New York City police raid on Stonewall Inn sparked riots and demonstrations in the surrounding streets that lasted several nights. These events catalyzed a nationwide movement that united gay and lesbian people in the push for equal rights for all people, regardless of sexual orientation or identity. During OHNY Weekend, visit the site where the modern struggle for civil rights of gay and lesbian Americans began.

On Saturday and Sunday, join a ranger-led walking tour around Stonewall National Monument in Greenwich Village to learn about the history of the Stonewall Uprising and its importance to the gay civil rights movement.

All Weekend, the Stonewall National Monument Visitor Center—the first LGBTQ+ visitor center within the National Park Service—opens to the public for drop-in visits. OHNY Weekend visitors are invited to explore the historic site at their own pace or join guided tours on a first-come, first-served basis.

An incomparable educational resource, the visitor center offers an immersive experience featuring a rich tapestry of LGBTQ+ history and culture through compelling exhibitions and inspiring visual art displays. Visitors are introduced to a multifaceted experience that speaks across generations, encouraging all to carry forward the Stonewall legacy and the ongoing fight for full LGBTQ+ equality.
sites.short: Explore the birthplace of the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement with ranger-led walking tours and self-guided visits at the Stonewall National Monument, including access to the first LGBTQ+ visitor center within the National Park Service, featuring immersive exhibits and inspiring art displays.

sites.name: Sunset Park Open Studios
sites.description:
Sunset Park Open Studios (SPOS) is an annual multi-day event featuring open studios, exhibitions, performances, and cultural programming, free and open to all. SPOS is committed to bridging artists with residents, institutions, and visitors, and fostering authentic relationships that center the neighborhood's unique history, diversity, and identity. Every fall this weekend brings visitors from all over the city to Sunset Park as a waterfront destination in celebration of the arts, culture, and history.

SPOS was born in 2019 from a shared belief: that the artists of Sunset Park deserved a spotlight in their own neighborhood. Founded by the NARS Foundation in collaboration with a coalition of local arts organizations, SPOS began as a grassroots celebration, an open invitation for the neighborhood to step inside its studios, meet its makers, and witness their creative work.

Each year, SPOS has expanded its reach, drawing hundreds of visitors into the heart of Sunset Park and revealing the neighborhood's emergence as one of Brooklyn's most vital arts districts. In 2023, Sunset Park Wide Open was established as an independent nonprofit to carry this work forward with greater intention and capacity. SPWO took stewardship of SPOS and committed to building on its founding spirit: collaborative and accessible to the neighborhood it serves.

sites.name: Surrogate's Courthouse
sites.description:
Surrogate's Courthouse, on the northwest corner of Chambers and Centre Streets, houses the Surrogate's Court and was originally built as the city's Hall of Records. Planned in 1888 and constructed from 1899 to 1907 at a cost of over $7 million, it was designed by John R. Thomas and completed after his death by Horgan & Slattery. Built of granite over a fire-resistant steel frame, the seven-story building was renamed Surrogate's Courthouse in 1962.

A Beaux-Arts landmark of the City Beautiful movement, the building features a triple-arched entrance with thirty-six-foot Corinthian columns and a mansard roof. Considered by Thomas to be his masterpiece, its grand marble staircase and rotunda were inspired by the Paris Opera House. The exterior carries 54 allegorical sculptures by Philip Martiny and Henry K. Bush-Brown, while muralist William DeLeftwich Dodge created the interior zodiac mosaics. The ornate courtrooms feature gilded plaster, carved mahogany and oak paneling, and an interior courtyard rising from the first to fourth floors beneath a skylight.

A designated New York City Landmark, Surrogate's Courthouse anchors the Civic Center across from City Hall Park and remains a frequent filming location.

During OHNY Weekend, visitors will see the building's Beaux-Arts interior up close, including the marble staircase, zodiac mosaics, and richly decorated courtrooms, and learn about the City Beautiful movement that shaped its design and the architects and artists who brought it to life.
sites.short: Step inside a Beaux-Arts masterpiece to explore its grand marble staircase, zodiac mosaics, and lavish courtrooms, while discovering the stories behind its celebrated architects, artists, and the City Beautiful movement that inspired its design.

sites.name: Temple Emanu-El and Bernard Museum of Judaica
sites.description:
Built in the Modern Romanesque style popular in the late 1920s, Temple Emanu-El is one of the largest houses of worship in the world and the oldest Reform synagogue in New York City. The sanctuary features dazzling mosaics by noted muralist Hildreth Meière, an intricately painted ceiling, and towering stained glass windows. The building's meticulous decorative restoration by Beyer Blinder Belle received the New York Landmarks Conservancy's Lucy G. Moses Preservation Award in 2007. 

Temple Emanu-El is one of the country’s first synagogues to amass its own Judaica collection, which now contains 1,700 objects that showcase Jewish Heritage in the Herbert & Eileen Bernard Museum, housed within the synagogue building. The permanent collection spans centuries and continents, from medieval Europe to objects made by Jews living in Muslim lands, Tiffany windows to 21st century Judaica.

During OHNY Weekend, sanctuary docents will lead optional guided tours of the synagogue.

sites.description:
**Booking this experience is a two-step process**. Review the "Policies" section below for full details.

The MADE Show by Normal New York is a special edition of the Not-A-Normal Show, created in partnership with MADE Bush Terminal. Centered around Makers, Artists, Designers & Entrepreneurs, the three-day show brings together approximately 50 independent vendors in Sunset Park.

Founded by Normal New York, Not-A-Normal Show is a curated retail and cultural platform known for bringing independent designers, vintage dealers, artists, and creative businesses together inside some of New York City’s most distinctive spaces. Since 2024, the show has activated former Barneys New York, One Hanson Place, Manhattan Mall, and other unexpected venues, welcoming tens of thousands of visitors while creating physical platforms for thousands of independent businesses.

The MADE Show builds on that mission with a more accessible, community-driven format specifically centered on makers, artists, designers, and entrepreneurs. Approximately 45 businesses will come together for three days of independent retail alongside live making and artist demonstrations, creative programming, local food and beverage, and community-focused activations. Visitors are invited not only to shop, but to meet the people behind the work, see creative processes unfold, and discover what is being made by independent businesses today.

The partnership with MADE Bush Terminal brings the concept into a site rooted in New York’s history of industry and production and now being reimagined for contemporary manufacturing and creative enterprise. Normal New York is the creator, curator, and producer of The MADE Show, presented in partnership with MADE Bush Terminal.
sites.short: Experience a day of independent shopping, live maker and artist demonstrations, creative workshops, and community events, with a chance to meet the creators and see their work in action—all hosted in a historic industrial space reimagined for today’s creative entrepreneurs.

sites.name: The Peninsula
sites.description:
The Peninsula is a new mixed-use campus in Hunts Point that transforms the former Spofford Juvenile Detention Center into a vibrant neighborhood destination. The project brings together 740 permanently affordable homes, 50,000 square feet of light industrial space, community amenities, and a large open space campus.

On the tour, visitors will explore how architecture and urban design have transformed a formerly isolated site into a connected part of Hunts Point. Step streets, public gardens, landscaped plazas, and pedestrian pathways weave between new buildings, creating places for gathering and community life. Visitors will also have the opportunity to see the residential amenities that contribute to the quality of the affordable homes.

The Peninsula is the result of decades of community advocacy and collaboration among local organizations, public agencies, developers, and designers. WXY served as the project’s architecture and urban design firm alongside Body Lawson Associates and Elizabeth Kennedy Landscape Architect, helping shape a campus that brings housing, jobs, culture, and public space together in the heart of Hunts Point.

The tour will be led by Jacob Dugopolski, Associate Principal, Anna Hajdo, Senior Associate, and Maggie Musante, Architectural Designer, of WXY

sites.name: The People’s Theatre: Centro Cultural Inmigrante
sites.description:
For eighteen years, The People's Theatre (formerly the People's Theatre Project) staged its immigrant, multilingual programming in borrowed venues across the city. Opening September 2026 on West 206th Street, this 19,000-square-foot center in Inwood gives the company its first permanent home—New York City's first immigrant-centered performing arts center, and the largest Latine-operated performing arts institution in New York State.

Designed by WORKac, the center occupies the ground floor and cellar of The Miramar, a new residential tower, and grew out of a 2021 public RFP tied to the Inwood rezoning. The design draws on Inwood's own visual identity—bodega storefronts, street art, the nearby Seaman Drake Arch—reimagined through the neighborhood's Art Deco lobbies, a style the architects describe as a "vernacular modernism" for the Global South.

Visitors enter through the "Rampatorium," a continuous ramp-as-lobby whose shifting levels double as seating for thirty to forty people, ensuring everyone arrives the same way. Five street-facing studios, including the Ernesto Concepción Studio Theatre, make rehearsals and classes visible from the sidewalk, while the Mainstage Theatre, engineered as a "box within a box" for acoustic isolation, reconfigures across twenty-five filed seating layouts, from proscenium to full black box.

Guests will experience the bold, color-driven interiors, custom wallpapers, and Art Deco tilework that carry the organization's identity throughout, and see how a publicly financed civic building became a home for Inwood's Latine and immigrant communities.
sites.short: Explore a vibrant new performing arts center featuring bold, Art Deco-inspired interiors, flexible theaters, and street-facing studios that showcase rehearsals and classes to the public, all designed to celebrate and serve immigrant and Latine communities in a welcoming, innovative space.

The Riverie, a mixed-use waterfront development in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, designed by Marvel, aims to redefine urban living. With over 800 rental units, 30% of which are affordable housing, and 13,000+ square feet of retail space, it  blends community life with sustainability. Using a geothermal system, the largest of its kind in New York State residential projects, it targets significant reductions of carbon emissions. 

During OHNY Weekend, visitors will be able to access a wide variety of units, see some of the geothermal system in action, and explore many of the amenities across the block-wide site. End the tour with a visit to the waterfront public park designed by Field Operations as part of the project. Tours will be led by Dennis Vermeulen, Partner, and Manche Mitchell, Associate, from Marvel, as well as team members from INC.

sites.description:
"On October 27, 1858, I was born at No. 28 East Twentieth Street, New York City, in the house in which we lived during the time that my two sisters and my brother and I were small children." — Theodore Roosevelt

During OHNY Weekend, visit the recreated home of our 26th President, Theodore Roosevelt, where he lived until he was 15 years old. Step into his childhood as you tour five historic period rooms that feature original furnishings.

sites.name: THWACK at the Brooklyn Army Terminal
sites.partner: Mmuseumm and NYC Economic Development Corporation
sites.description:
Ride the NYC Ferry across New York Harbor to a former military campus along Brooklyn's working waterfront and discover "THWACK: 26 Glorious Gadgets and Gizmos of Production," a surprising art exhibit inside a vacant 30,000-square-foot warehouse. Upon entering the massive space at the Brooklyn Army Terminal (BAT), participants will be surrounded by 26 towering photographic portraits transforming the industrial warehouse into an extraordinary public art experience. 

Rather than depicting people, the portraits capture the humble and hard-worn tools used by the diverse range of craftspeople at BAT who manufacture everything from springs to ice cream cones to rocket ship parts. The diversity of everyday objects created along the Sunset Park waterfront is awe-inspiring. At the same time, the historic military and manufacturing campus can feel vast, impenetrable, and enigmatic, concealing from public view the people, stories, and craftsmanship that flourish inside its walls.

The new free exhibition, presented by BAT and Mmuseumm, offers visitors a lyrical and breathtaking step into the beauty of how things are made. It serves as an ode to the worker’s tools, finding awe in the process, crafts, and people driving one of New York City’s largest manufacturing campuses.
sites.short: Step inside a vast warehouse space to experience a striking art exhibit featuring giant photographic portraits of the tools used by craftspeople at the Brooklyn waterfront campus, offering a unique glimpse into the world of local manufacturing and the artistry behind everyday objects.
sites.access_notes: If arriving by NYC Ferry, the exhibit is located directly across from the Sunset Park/Brooklyn Army Terminal landing, in Building A. If arriving by other forms of transportation, guests may access the exhibit by taking the ramp just south of 58th Street down to the pier level.

Since 1931, Tom’s Sons has been a family-owned fabric and textile pleating business. This full-service facility is located in the heart of New York City’s Garment District and offers all aspects of pleating services, from sample development to production. Tom's Sons has become a trusted collaborator for iconic fashion brands like Oscar de la Renta, Coach, Vera Wang, and Ralph Lauren, as well as major productions like the Met Gala, Hollywood films, and Broadway productions.
sites.short: Go behind the scenes of a renowned pleating workshop, explore the craft’s rich family legacy, and see firsthand how pleats are created for top fashion houses and major stage and screen productions.

Tom's Sons is an active working factory, so visitors should expect a functioning production environment with machinery, grease and oil, and occasional noise. Closed-toe shoes are recommended and visitors should be mindful of the equipment.

Hear from dedicated volunteers about the restoration work to get this 1933 steamship running again. View a display commemorating the 9/11 Boatlift--the biggest evacuation by water in American history.

sites.description:
UrbanGlass, a nonprofit established in 1977, fosters experimentation and advances the use and critical understanding of glass as a creative medium.  From introductory lessons taught by distinguished teachers from across the United States to master-level intensives led by internationally acclaimed artists, UrbanGlass’ year-round educational programming provides a space to explore this incredible material through hands-on and experiential learning. The facility houses studios where New Yorkers can learn techniques for glassblowing, neon, kiln-formed glass, stained glass, and more! 

During OHNY Weekend, visitors can tour the space and enjoy the artwork in the on-site store and gallery, which highlights innovative glass art and design.
sites.short: Tour working glass studios, view cutting-edge glass art in the gallery, and experience hands-on demonstrations in glassblowing, neon, and more.

sites.name: Vagelos Innovation Laboratories
sites.description:
The first purpose-built, all-electric academic research lab building in New York City, the Vagelos Innovation Laboratories expands Columbia University’s research capacity with laboratory and office space. Designed to use significantly less energy than similar buildings of its kind, the Vagelos Innovation Laboratories performs 30% more efficiently than the ASHRAE 90.1 2010 standard and outperforms the emission limits set by New York City’s Local Law 97. The project aligns with the University’s Plan 2030 climate goals to introduce no new fossil fuel infrastructure into campus buildings. 

Rising eight stories, the building houses biomedical research and lab facilities, as well as symposium and community engagement spaces. Attendees will learn how the design and engineering team balanced the intensive mechanical needs of the lab typology with ambitious sustainability goals and delivered a project that will help unlock decarbonization for Columbia University’s medical campus. 

This tour will be led by Gabriel Morales, KPF Senior Associate Principal, and will offer an opportunity to walk through the building just weeks after its opening!

Founded in 1817, the campus is home to some of the most intricate and historically significant architectural features of any higher education campus in New York, characterized by detailed stonework, vaulted ceilings, stained glass, and high windows.

OHNY Weekend attendees will be able to visit this urban oasis on one of Manhattan’s most special blocks and explore interior and exterior portions of the 2.7 acre historic campus through self-guided tours. Architects who have led past renovations and who are planning for future updates will be on-site to answer questions and highlight the design choices that preserve historic character while welcoming a new chapter for the building and for Vanderbilt University in New York City.

sites.description: The mission of Village Community Boathouse (VCB) is to improve public access to urban waterways and to introduce the public, especially young people, to the joys of rowing in New York Harbor. VCB members revive the art of small boat seamanship and boatbuilding, advance the environmental stewardship of the estuary, and foster a tradition of maritime hospitality and fellowship. From the beginning, VCB has been dedicated to free community rowing and to youth rowing programs for local high schools and colleges, including Stuyvesant High School, the New York Harbor School. During OHNY Weekend, visitors will be able to explore the VCB wood shop and see what it takes to build a boat and what's involved in fleet maintenance.

sites.name: Voelker Orth Museum
sites.description:
The Voelker Orth Museum, Bird Sanctuary, and Victorian Garden was home to three generations of a German immigrant family. They came to Queens for a comfortable middle-class life when NYC was growing into a modern metropolis. The property has retained its 1890s-1930s appearance and welcomes visitors year-round. There’s a house tour, art and art-making, and a Victorian-styled garden to enjoy. 

The exhibition "All the Queens Gardens: Documentary Photography by Rafael Herrin-Ferri" will be on view for OHNY Weekend visitors, including a selection of images from Rafael Herrin-Ferri’s book, All the Queens Gardens, a study on garden landscapes by home gardeners in Queens. The images showcase the borough’s multiculturalism through urban gardening efforts, from Hindu courtyards and Chinese vegetable gardens to French-style lawns, fountains and painted sidewalks.
sites.short: Visit a preserved historic home and explore original 1890s-1930s interiors, hands-on art activities, and a lush Victorian garden, all set within a tranquil bird sanctuary.

General printed information about the Museum is available in Chinese, English, Korean and Spanish, as well as large print.

sites.name: Wagner Park
sites.description:
Wagner Park sits at the southern edge of Battery Park City, where the Hudson meets New York Harbor. Long known for its sweeping views of the Statue of Liberty, the park has been transformed into one of the city’s most advanced examples of climate resilient design.

The landscape now rises in terraces that double as flood barriers, protecting Lower Manhattan while preserving lawns and gathering spaces for the public. Salvaged stone and wood from the original park, permeable paving, native planting, and solar powered lighting all speak to a sustainable future rooted in thoughtful design. That integration of resilience, landscape, and public space was recently recognized with a 2026 AIA New York Merit Award in Urban Design.

On this tour led by Gonzalo Cruz, Vice President and Design Principal of AECOM LAUD NYC, visitors will see how infrastructure and landscape can work as one. The project team will share how designers and engineers collaborated to turn flood protection into a public asset, ensuring Wagner Park remains open, green, and resilient.
sites.short: Explore innovative climate-resilient design while touring terraced landscapes that serve as both flood barriers and public gathering spaces, featuring sustainable materials and solar lighting, with insights from the project team on transforming infrastructure into a community asset.

Join Ken Soehner, Arthur K. Watson Chief Librarian, for a private tour of the Library’s public spaces, including the newly renovated Nolen Study Room and the closed library stacks, which are not normally open to visitors. The tour will end in the Book Conservation Lab with a look at books from the special collections.

sites.name: Westbeth Artists Housing
sites.description:
Westbeth is the largest live/work space for artists in the country. Originally built by Bell Laboratories, a company known for its innovative products developed here, the complex's renovation into space for artists was one of architect Richard Meier’s first commissions and was one of the earliest adaptive reuse projects in NYC.

During OHNY Weekend, hour-long historic tours are offered of the building, with details on Bell Labs and Westbeth’s artist community. Visitors can also explore dozens of artists studios, as well as spaces devoted to the creation and presentation of art by resident and guest artists. The Westbeth courtyard will host an Art, Craft and Vintage Market as well, with live music.
sites.short: Go behind the scenes with guided tours of a landmark artist community, explore rarely accessible studios and creative spaces, and enjoy an outdoor market featuring art, crafts, vintage finds, and live music.

sites.name: William Ulmer Brewery
sites.description:
The William Ulmer Brewery is a 19th-century, individually landmarked brewery in Brooklyn, designed by Theobald Engelhardt and considered one of the last remaining and best-maintained examples of pre-Prohibition brewery architecture in the borough. The building's original seven levels were designed around a gravity-fed brewing system, with raw ingredients entering at the top floor and moving down through each stage of production; the deepest of its three cellar levels features vaulted ceilings originally used for cold storage.

DXA Studio is renovating the building into a 40,000-square-foot mixed-use project, restoring the original brick façades and introducing contemporary interventions that speak to its brewing history. Visitors will join a guided tour led by Shane Phelan, Associate, and Josh Kayden, Intermediate Designer III, of DXA and see how a historic industrial building is being adapted at close range: the treatment of the original brick masonry, the building's gravity-fed floor plan and vaulted cellar levels, and how the design distinguishes new residential floors from the ground-level commercial space while preserving the structure's industrial character.
sites.short: Join an architect-led tour to explore the restoration of a landmark 19th-century brewery, including its vaulted cellar levels, and the innovative blend of historic and contemporary design elements.

sites.name: Williamsburg Biannual
sites.description: The Williamsburg Biannual is a purpose-built nonprofit artist space in Brooklyn, New York. Located steps from the Williamsburg Bridge and Domino Park, the WB’s home is an adaptive reuse and expansion of a 1920s 10,000-square-foot warehouse, designed by JAZ Architect. The Biannual’s premises include public gathering space, a black box event space, double-height galleries, and a private outdoor space. Natural light permeates throughout the building, creating a serene environment and an urban oasis. An exhibition of artwork by renowned artist and educator Lisa Corrinne Davis will be on view during OHNY Weekend.
sites.short: Visit an urban oasis for contemporary art in a beautifully repurposed warehouse featuring serene natural light and exclusive access to a private outdoor space, with opportunities to view works by acclaimed artist Lisa Corrinne Davis.

sites.name: WindScape Brooklyn Port Tour
sites.description:
WindScape Brooklyn is proud to present the inaugural OHNY Weekend Tour of the Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Base and South Brooklyn Marine Terminal (SBMT), which will serve New York City's first offshore wind project, Empire Wind. Located 15-30 miles off the coast of Long Island, the project's 54 turbines will power approximately 500,000 homes upon completion. 

This tour will allow participants to step onto a section of the largest offshore wind port in the United States, see the project’s large-scale infrastructure from a closer vantage point, and walk around the exterior of the O&M base that will serve Empire Wind through its three-decade lifespan. This is a once-in-a-generation project, built by local labor, that will help NYC and New York meet their renewable energy targets. Following the tour of the port, visitors will be able to explore WindScape Brooklyn’s interactive offshore wind exhibits.

Port tours will be led by Ana Fisyak, Executive Director, WindScape Brooklyn. Following the tour of the port, visitors will be able to explore the WindScape exhibition.
sites.short: Get an exclusive look inside the nation’s largest offshore wind port, and tour the exterior of the operations and maintenance base that will power a landmark renewable energy project.

sites.name: Woolworth Lobby - Saturday
sites.description:
The Woolworth was the tallest building in the world from its opening in 1913 until it was overtaken by the nearby Bank of Manhattan building at 40 Wall Street in 1930. Nicknamed the "Cathedral of Commerce" for its opulent lobby resembling a grand cathedral, the Woolworth is one of the first modern skyscrapers. 

Built under the direction of Cass Gilbert, one of America’s most important architects, and a team of experts, the Woolworth is an engineering feat that changed the face of engineering for decades to come. During OHNY Weekend, get a rare chance to visit the building's iconic lobby with Woolworth Building expert Bob Gelber.
sites.short: Step inside the stunning, cathedral-like lobby of Cass Gilbert's "Cathedral of Commerce"—rarely open to the general public—and experience the grandeur of this pioneering skyscraper that once reigned as the world's tallest building.
sites.access_notes:
Some areas of the lobby are only accessible by stairs, and elevator access is not available. No strollers, large bags, or pets permitted in the lobby.

Children are welcome, accompanied by an adult. All participants, including children, must have a ticket.

sites.name: Yankee Ferry - Saturday
sites.description:
The "Yankee," also known as "Machigonne," is a historic steel-hulled ferry. Described as unusually luxurious for a day-voyaging vessel, Yankee was built in 1907 by the Philadelphia shipbuilding company Neafie & Levy for the Casco Bay and Harpswell Line. Today, it's the last surviving Ellis Island ferry and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1992.

The ferry initially transported wealthy vacationers between locations like Portland, Maine, and the Calendar Islands, and later between Boston and Pine Island. During World War I, it was commissioned by the U.S. Navy, stripped of its luxury features, and used as an offshore patrol boat with cannons. After the war, the ferry was relocated to New York Harbor and began its service transporting immigrants to Ellis Island. The Yankee was also one of the first ferries to carry passengers to Liberty Island when it opened to the public. 

In 1990, the by-now dilapidated Yankee was bought by a private citizen, Jim Gallagher, who began working on its restoration. In 2001, artists Victoria and Richard MacKenzie-Childs (founders and designers of the home furnishing company MacKenzie-Childs Ltd.) purchased the ferry and have transformed the boat into a livable work of art while also continuing its restoration. With the construction of the Hudson River Park, the ferry was displaced to Hoboken, New Jersey, then moved to Red Hook, Brooklyn, and is now on Staten Island.
sites.short: Step aboard a beautifully restored, historic ferry that once transported immigrants to Ellis Island and was among the first to carry visitors to Liberty Island, now transformed into a unique floating work of art by renowned designers.
